plan.hypothesis: Decreasing control/recipe/holding_tip_speed_weight from the source value 0.05 to its domain lower bound 0.025 on the T0-template configuration under the fixed controller.gvs_nmpc@10.0.0 will lower holding_max_speed_m_s below the 0.02 m/s acceptance bound while keeping terminal_error_m and holding_max_error_m below 0.01 m, force_bound_violation_n at 0.0 N and a finite valid complete execution, thereby attaining joint nominal reach-and-hold acceptance.
plan.rationale: Control-only research is legitimate and the recipe tip-speed weights are the only legal continuous control paths. The joint failure is a held-speed failure, and terminal_tip_speed_weight is saturated at its 0.1 upper bound, leaving control/recipe/holding_tip_speed_weight as the usable lever. The source configuration batch-0497cdd238512a92-0 is distinct from the latest tested candidate (batch-67047ea375b20a2c-1) and the retained baseline (fixed-radius), yet sits on the same T0 template, so the comparison isolates the weight change. Because only one development execution remains, a deterministic one-point explicit enumeration at the lower domain bound 0.025 is chosen over an uncontrolled coordinate proposal that could step upward. Every point must produce a complete evaluation with force bounds and a finite valid execution before any claim, and no cross-template routing scale is reapplied.

arguments.reasoning: Feedback-first on the current completed evaluation (status completed F1480, stop_reason proposal_limit F1356): it is a valid_failure (F1467) with accepted=false (F1434). Terminal reach passes (F1360) and holding position passes (F1444, holding_max_error 0.00308 m, F1382), and the run is a finite valid complete execution with zero solver errors and no force-bound violation (F1387 true, F1475 0, F1428 0.0 N). The single binding deficiency is held tip speed: holding_speed_passed=false (F1365) with holding_max_speed 0.03828 m/s (F1438), above the 0.02 m/s bound, so joint_reach_holding_passed=false (F1400) and the terminal error (F1460 0.00292 m) is already inside 0.01 m. The only legal continuous levers are the two recipe tip-speed weights; terminal_tip_speed_weight is saturated at its 0.1 upper bound and cannot be increased, so the usable continuous lever is control/recipe/holding_tip_speed_weight in [0.025, 0.1]. Across the available controller10 T0-template evidence the source configuration (batch-0497cdd238512a92-0, holding weight 0.05) records a substantially smaller held-window speed (~0.0219 m/s in the bound ledger) than the latest tested point (holding 0.06875, 0.03828 m/s, F1438), i.e. in the sampled range a LOWER holding_tip_speed_weight gave a LOWER held speed. I therefore branch from that source and probe the lower domain at holding_tip_speed_weight=0.025, a one-point explicit test of whether decreasing the weight clears the 0.02 m/s hold bound while preserving terminal/holding position, force bounds and a finite valid execution. Direction control matters because only one development execution remains, so a single deterministic enumeration is preferred over an uncontrolled coordinate proposal that could step upward.
unresolved_uncertainties: Whether decreasing holding_tip_speed_weight actually lowers held tip speed under controller.gvs_nmpc@10.0.0 rather than merely relaxing a penalty.
Whether the residual held speed is control-weight-limited or physical/structure-limited.
